# Introduction and problem statement

CampusPulse is a student-outcome analytics case study using the UCI *Predict Students' Dropout and Academic Success* dataset. The target categories are Dropout, Enrolled and Graduate. The project compares two classification algorithms under two feature-availability scenarios and uses feature importance and LIME to interpret model behaviour. It is a decision-support exercise, not a definitive judgement about an individual student.

# Dataset and preparation

The UCI dataset contains 4,424 records, 36 predictors and one target column. The original CSV is comma-separated. The analysis uses the UCI source URL directly and standardises column names with `janitor::clean_names()`. The cleaned dataset used in the completed analysis had no missing values.

# Exploratory analysis

Recorded target distribution:

| Outcome | Students | Percentage |
|---|---:|---:|
| Dropout | 1,421 | 32.12% |
| Enrolled | 794 | 17.95% |
| Graduate | 2,209 | 49.91% |

Recorded group averages:

| Outcome | Average age at enrolment | Admission grade | First-semester grade |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Dropout | 26.1 | 125.0 | 7.26 |
| Enrolled | 22.4 | 126.0 | 11.1 |
| Graduate | 21.8 | 129.0 | 12.6 |

These are descriptive associations, not causal findings.

# Prediction scenarios and models

- **Scenario A:** admission-time/background information; first- and second-semester features excluded.
- **Scenario B:** Scenario A plus first-semester academic information; second-semester features excluded.

The algorithms are Multinomial Logistic Regression and Random Forest. Performance is evaluated using accuracy, macro precision, macro recall, macro F1 and confusion matrices.

# Recorded results

| Scenario | Model | Accuracy | Macro precision | Macro recall | Macro F1 |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| A | Multinomial Logistic Regression | 64.21% | 56.08% | 53.59% | 53.25% |
| A | Random Forest | 65.80% | 59.25% | 54.24% | 52.95% |
| B | Multinomial Logistic Regression | 73.61% | 65.52% | 63.92% | 63.84% |
| B | Random Forest | 74.97% | 68.72% | 64.13% | 63.90% |

Scenario B Random Forest had the highest recorded accuracy (74.97%) and macro F1 (63.90%). Adding first-semester data increased accuracy by 9.17 percentage points for Random Forest and 9.40 percentage points for Logistic Regression.

## Class-wise evaluation

Scenario B Random Forest confusion matrix (rows = predicted; columns = actual):

| Predicted / Actual | Dropout | Enrolled | Graduate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Dropout | 227 | 52 | 27 |
| Enrolled | 16 | 34 | 13 |
| Graduate | 41 | 72 | 401 |

Class recall: Dropout 79.93%, Enrolled 21.52%, Graduate 90.93%. The low Enrolled recall is a major limitation and shows why overall accuracy alone is insufficient.

## Feature importance and LIME

Recorded top Scenario B Random Forest features:

| Feature | Importance |
|---|---:|
| First-semester approved curricular units | 337.54 |
| First-semester grade | 219.15 |
| Course | 162.96 |
| Father's occupation | 130.39 |
| Tuition fees up to date | 111.06 |

LIME was applied to one selected Scenario B Random Forest prediction. The model predicted Dropout with a score of approximately 86.16%. The strongest positive local contributions included tuition-fee status (+0.2567) and approved first-semester curricular units (+0.2055). This explanation is local to one selected case and is not causal.

# Conclusion, limitations and future work

CampusPulse demonstrates a complete workflow for student-outcome classification using R. Scenario B Random Forest achieved the strongest recorded overall metrics. However, its Enrolled-class recall was only 21.52%, so the model requires improvement before any operational use. The dataset may not represent every institution; feature importance and LIME do not establish causation; and predictions should support human review rather than automate high-impact decisions.

Future work includes improving Enrolled-class recognition, using repeated cross-validation and external validation, and evaluating probability calibration with domain experts.
